nodes.label: The incoming/ staging tree
nodes.rationale: Four post-mirror Drive folders, 54 small files that MANIFEST.tsv does not cover. Not the mirror and no manifest rows: a staging area for content pulled through the connector when drive_sync.py could not run for want of OAuth credentials. Once a credentialed sync runs these land under drive/ and this tree can be dropped.

nodes.label: Assembly From .partNN Pieces
nodes.rationale: Both forms are kept - the parts are the byte-exact Drive records and the whole file sits beside them, concatenated in index order. Every split was contiguous from part00 and assembly is reproducible by concatenation alone. HANDOFF-152 carries independent proof: it records r2-32a.py at 22,360 B / 15a9047a before these parts existed, and concatenating the five Drive parts reproduces that size and md5 exactly.

nodes.label: The Base64-Through-Conversation Cost
nodes.rationale: The connector returns content as base64 inside the conversation, so every byte is spent as model context and transcribed back out. Affordable for three small files; roughly 200,000 tokens with a real chance of a typo for the remaining ~51 to move 185 KB. A Drive mount does it in one command because the bytes never pass through a model.

nodes.label: Verification by Drive's Own fileSize
nodes.rationale: Every file kept here was verified by byte count against Drive's own fileSize - the check that caught both wrong uploads in BUILD183, and weaker than an md5 read-back.
